key: And the believers should not all go out to fight. Of every troop of them, a party only should go forth, that they (who are left behind) may gain sound knowledge in religion, and that they may warn their folk when they return to them, so that they may beware.
s: In a chapter that commands fighting and condemns staying behind, the believers learn who must march; al-Tabari, on 9:121 to 9:122, takes the understanding as gained by the party that marches, not by those who stay, from seeing God’s victory for the believers.

evidence.words: فإن أولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب، قولُ من قال: ليتفقه الطائفة النافرة بما تعاين من نصر الله أهلَ دينه وأصحابَ رسوله، على أهل عداوته والكفر به … فإن قال قائل: وما تنكر أن يكون معناه: ليتفقه المتخلِّفون في الدين؟ قيل: ننكر ذلك لاستحالته.
evidence.gloss: The most correct of the views is that of whoever said: let the party that marches out gain understanding by what it witnesses of God’s giving victory to the people of His religion and the companions of His Messenger over those hostile to Him and disbelieving in Him ... If someone asks, why do you reject that it means ‘so that those who stay behind may gain understanding in religion’, the answer is: we reject it because it is impossible.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, At-Tawbah 9:122, at 1356). Plain sense faithful: 9:120 condemns staying behind the messenger, 9:122 says not all believers should go out, a party from each troop; no four-word run from the ayah. al-Tabari’s comment is one segment on 9:121 to 9:122 and is cited as such. After reporting the views (the stayers learn, per Qatada and one Ibn Abbas report; the marchers learn, per al-Hasan), he states his own preference: the marching party gains understanding by witnessing God’s victory for His people over the idolaters, and he rejects the stayers reading as impossible. The sentence carries this preference, attributed where he states it; it departs from Pickthall’s parenthesis ‘(who are left behind)’, which is the translator’s addition, and the reading is al-Tabari’s, not the translator’s. Evidence copied from the packet with an ellipsis between two verbatim pieces. entry-check ok.
